Functions to filter data

The following code chunk creates the functions to filter data based on the user input. This is not used for the rest of this exercise, but will be utilised in the shiny app to pre-filter the dataset before perfoming the computations/displaying the graph.

  • Transaction type
  • Customer type
  • Transaction Date Range
filter_tx <- function(selected_type='All'){
 if(selected_type!='All'){
    result <- transactions %>%
      filter(type==selected_type)
    return(result)
 }
  else {
    return(transactions)
  }
}

filter_customer <- function(selected_type='All', selected_value='All'){
  if(selected_type!='All'){
      selected_cols <- customers %>%
          select(customer_id, all_of(selected_type), first_tx)
      if (!identical(selected_value, 'All')){
        filtered_customers <- selected_cols %>%
          filter(.data[[selected_type]] %in% selected_value)
      return(filtered_customers)
    } else {
      return(selected_cols)
    }
  }
  else{
    return(select(customers, customer_id, first_tx))
  }
}

filter_tx_dates<- function(tx=transactions, start_date, end_date){
   result <- tx %>%
     filter(date>=ymd(start_date),
            date<=ymd(end_date))%>%
     mutate(week = yearweek(date),
            wk_date=as.Date(week))
   
   return(result)
}

Cohort Retention Analysis

Filter Shiny widget type Values Function
Customer segment filter Radio buttons
  • ‘All’
  • Values of variable used to segment customer base
 Allow users to toggle cohort retention analysis of specific segments to facilitate comparison 
get_cohort_data <- function(tx_df, cust_df, selected_type, segment_value){
  if (segment_value != 'All'){
    cust_data <- cust_df %>%
      filter(.data[[selected_type]] == segment_value)
  }
  else{
    cust_data <- cust_df
  }
  result <- tx_df %>%
    inner_join(cust_data, by = "customer_id")%>%
    mutate(
      cohort_month = floor_date(as.Date(first_tx), "month"),
      activity_month = floor_date(as.Date(date), "month"),
      month_number = (year(activity_month) - year(cohort_month)) * 12 + 
                 (month(activity_month) - month(cohort_month))
    )
}

get_cra_heatmap <- function(cra_data, selected_type, segment_value) {
  
    cohort_counts <- cra_data %>%
    group_by(cohort_month, month_number) %>%
    summarise(active_users = n_distinct(customer_id), .groups = 'drop')
  
    initial_cohorts <- cohort_counts %>%
      filter(month_number == 0) %>%
      select(cohort_month, initial_users = active_users)
    
    retention_matrix <- cohort_counts %>%
      left_join(initial_cohorts, by = "cohort_month") %>%
      mutate(retention_pct = active_users / initial_users)
    
    if (segment_value=='All'){
      title_value=paste("Customer Retention by Acquisition Cohort (", 
                        selected_type, "-", segment_value, ")")
    } else{
      title_value=("Customer Retention by Acquisition Cohort")
    }
    
    result <- ggplot(retention_matrix, aes(x = month_number, y = factor(cohort_month), fill = retention_pct)) +
      geom_tile() +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick",
                           mid = "white",
                          high = "steelblue",
                          midpoint = 0.5,
                          labels = scales::percent,
                          limits = c(0, 1)) +
      theme_grey() +
      labs(title = paste("Customer Retention by Acquisition Cohort (", selected_type, "-", segment_value, ")"),
           x = "Months Since Acquisition",
           y = "Acquisition Cohort",
           fill = "Retention Rate")
    return(result)
}
heatmap <- get_cra_heatmap(cohort_data, "clv_segment", "Bronze")
heatmap

get_seasonal_data <- function(tx_df, cust_df, segmentation){
  result <- tx_df %>%
    inner_join(cust_df, by = "customer_id") %>%
    group_by(date, !!sym(segmentation)) %>%
    summarise(tx_count = n(),
            tx_amt = sum(amount),
            user_count = n_distinct(customer_id),
            .groups = 'drop') %>%
    as_tsibble(index = date, 
               key = !!sym(segmentation))
}

Transaction behaviour over time

get_animation_data <- function(tx=transactions, cust=customers){
  result <- tx %>%
    inner_join(cust, by = "customer_id") %>%
    mutate(month = month(date)) %>%
    group_by(month, location) %>%
    summarise(
      avg_tx_value = mean(amount),
      avg_tx_count = n()/n_distinct(customer_id),
      unique_customers = n_distinct(customer_id),
      .groups = 'drop'
      )
}
# 1. Prepare Snapshot Data
# We aggregate by month and segment so each 'frame' has one dot per segment
animated_data <- transactions %>%
  inner_join(customers %>% select(customer_id, clv_segment), by = "customer_id") %>%
  mutate(month = month(date)) %>%
  group_by(month, clv_segment) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_tx_value = mean(amount),
    avg_tx_count = n()/n_distinct(customer_id),
    unique_customers = n_distinct(customer_id),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# 2. Build the Static ggplot
p <- ggplot(animated_data, aes(
    x = avg_tx_value, 
    y = avg_tx_count, 
    size = unique_customers
  )) +
  geom_point(aes(size=unique_customers, 
                  color = clv_segment,
                  ids = clv_segment,
                 frame=month),
             alpha = 0.7,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_grey() +
  labs(title = "User Transaction Behaviour over Time",
       x = "Average User Transaction Value",
       y = "Average User Transaction Counts")

Liquidity

Net Liquidity Visualisation

Data Preparation

First we will prepare the transaction data to represent inflows (deposits) and outflows (withdrawals). We take transfers as transfers made between accounts under the fintech company studied, hence we assume that the transfers do not affect the liquidity. Payments also not included

We will also create relevant columns to allow us to enhance the data visualisation later.

liquidity <- transactions %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, 
              values_from = amount,
              values_fn = sum) %>%
  replace_na(list(Withdrawal=0, Deposit=0)) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    Inflow=sum(Deposit),
    Outflow=sum(Withdrawal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = ifelse(Inflow > Outflow, "Inflow Higher", "Outflow Higher"),
         net_liquidity = Inflow-Outflow)

liquidity_wk <- transactions %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, 
              values_from = amount,
              values_fn = sum) %>%
  replace_na(list(Withdrawal=0, Deposit=0)) %>%
  mutate(week = yearweek(date),
         date=as.Date(week))%>%
  group_by(date, ) %>%
  summarise(
    Inflow=sum(Deposit),
    Outflow=sum(Withdrawal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = ifelse(Inflow > Outflow, "Inflow Higher", "Outflow Higher"),
         net_liquidity = Inflow-Outflow)
ggplot(liquidity_wk, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(Inflow, Outflow), 
                  ymax = pmax(Inflow, Outflow), 
                  fill = Group), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Inflow, color = "Inflow"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Outflow, color = "Outflow"), linewidth = 1) +
  # Styling
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Inflow" = "steelblue", "Outflow" = "coral")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Inflow Higher" = "steelblue", "Outflow Higher" = "coral")) +
  theme_grey() +
  labs(title = "Inflow vs. Outflow Over Time", 
       fill = "Net liquidity", color = "Series")

Forecasting

Split into training and test data

splits <- liquidity %>%
  initial_time_split(prop = 0.95)

Create models

model_fit_ets <- exp_smoothing() %>%
    set_engine(engine = "ets") %>%
    fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
        data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_arima <- arima_reg() %>%
  set_engine(engine = "auto_arima") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_arima_boosted <- arima_boost(
  min_n = 2,
  learn_rate = 0.015) %>%
  set_engine(
    engine = "auto_arima_xgboost") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))
frequency = 7 observations per 1 week
model_fit_prophet <- prophet_reg() %>%
  set_engine(engine = "prophet") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))

  set_engine("prophet_xgboost") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`), 
      data = training(splits))

model_fit_naive <- naive_reg() %>%
  set_engine("naive") %>%
  fit(net_liquidity ~ as.Date(`date`),
      data = training(splits))
model_spec_glmnet <- linear_reg(
    mixture = 0.9,
    penalty = 4.36e-6
) %>%
    set_engine("glmnet")
models_tbl <- modeltime_table(
  model_fit_ets,
  model_fit_arima,
  model_fit_arima_boosted,
  model_fit_prophet,
  model_fit_prophet_boost,
  model_fit_naive
)

Calibrate model to testing set

calibration_tbl <- models_tbl %>%
    modeltime_calibrate(new_data = testing(splits), quiet=FALSE)
model_fit_ensemble <- calibration_tbl %>%
  modeltime.ensemble::ensemble_average(type = "mean")
